items.title: A process model of stress generation in internalizing disorders
items.author: Joelle LeMoult
items.content: The stress generation model suggests that an individual’s characteristics can increase their chances of experiencing stressful life events. In this Perspective, Starr et al. detail the mechanistic processes of stress generation in people with internalizing psychopathology.

items.title: Approaches to differentiating the dimensions of social class
items.author: Kristin Laurin
items.content: Conflicting findings about the psychological effects of social class might arise because different operationalizations represent conceptually different constructs. In this Review, Laurin describes three approaches to studying social class and how each approach might help to account for conflicting findings.

items.title: Machine learning of digital traces to detect risk for behavioural addictions online
items.author: Vasileios Stavropoulos
items.content: Engaging in internet gaming, social media use and other online behaviours can become problematic, but these behaviours are not always clinically relevant. In this Review, Burleigh et al. describe how machine learning and psychological theories should be combined to identify people at risk of behavioural addictions.

items.title: The role of hippocampus-based developmental changes in paediatric post-traumatic stress disorder
items.author: Dylan G. Gee
items.content: The treatment of paediatric post-traumatic stress disorder currently focuses on associative processes that have primarily been studied in adults. In this Perspective, Foster et al. spotlight higher-order learning processes that typically develop during childhood to specify intervention targets for young patients.
